naming: The loader builds its YamlDotNet IDeserializer with CamelCaseNamingConvention + IgnoreUnmatchedProperties + AttemptingUnquotedStringTypeDeserialization (so template constants keep their scalar types). Enum values are parsed case-insensitively with '-'/'_' stripped. The template: block is a free-form object graph compiled by the loader, so its keys are the TARGET document's property names, not census keys; only the $-prefixed directive keys are dialect.

keys.description: The flow's unique identifier; seeds the stable FlowId. A blank value fails: "'name' is required for a translate flow."
Optional grouping label recorded with the run.

The flow's execution mode, read at the document envelope (YamlDocumentLoader's probe, FlowDocument.Mode) and projected to the catalog pipeline row. 'auto' (the default) runs on schedule fires and in batch/node group runs; 'manual' reserves a working flow for direct triggers; 'disabled' deactivates a retired one (a retired source, a run-once replay) with the same exclusions and a visible 'disabled' badge. A node-scoped run can opt into includeAll ('find all') to replay non-auto descendants deliberately, and naming a flow directly always runs it.
keys.validation: Unknown value fails to load: "<source>: 'mode' has unknown value '<value>'. Allowed: auto, manual, disabled."

keys.description: A development flow runs exactly like a production one but never generates notification events.
The document-local connection registry: each value is a connection string / ${...} reference, a map with 'provider' and 'connection', or bare (resolving ${env:SQLFLOW_CONN_<NAME>} by convention).
A connection name declared under 'connections:'. Exactly one of source.server / source.connection is required. The source must be SQL Server (mssql or azdb): the read is T-SQL.
A direct connection string or ${...} reference, registered under the synthesized name 'source'.
The provider of a direct connection. Anything but SQL Server is rejected at parse time.
The primary T-SQL query. Each row (documents.per: row) or the whole result set (resultSet) becomes one document. Column names must be unique and non-blank (alias computed columns).
keys.validation: The SQL is executed verbatim: SQLFlow performs no macro or parameter expansion here, so a token like @sf_watermark is an undefined T-SQL variable that fails the run. Only variables the query itself DECLAREs are usable.

keys.description: Named child result sets the template's $forEach arrays draw from. Each runs once per flow run against the source connection.
The dataset name $forEach references. Unique (case-insensitive); 'rows' is reserved for the primary query's rows.
The dataset's T-SQL query. Must return every bind column, or the run fails naming the missing columns.
keys.validation: Executed verbatim, exactly like source.query: no macro or parameter expansion; undeclared @-variables fail the run.

keys.description: The join columns matching a dataset row to its enclosing scope, compared by an invariant type-normalized form (int matches bigint; strings compare case-insensitively). Empty or absent declares a single-instance dataset that resolves to all of its rows at any scope: a one-row header for $row, or a global list for $forEach.

The document grain: one document per primary row (the row's columns are the root scope), or one for the whole result set (the primary rows are addressable as $forEach: rows; no columns in scope at the root).
Document-level null handling every leaf without its own $whenNull follows: omit drops the property, include emits an explicit JSON null.

The declared JSON shape. A mapping without $-keys is an object emitted verbatim; a sequence is a fixed array; a scalar with {Column} tokens is a templated string (a scalar that IS exactly one token passes the column's native JSON value through); any other scalar is a constant. {{ and }} escape literal braces; ${...} secret references pass through verbatim.
Directive leaf: emit the named source column's value (modified by $type/$format/$whenNull/$default). Exactly one of $column/$value/$template per directive node.

Directive leaf: a constant emitted verbatim (any YAML shape, scalar or structured). Cannot combine with $type/$whenNull/$default. Also the escape hatch for literal property names that start with '$' or collide with directives.
Directive leaf: a string built from literal text and {Column} tokens. When every referenced column is NULL the null policy applies instead of emitting the bare literal skeleton.

The JSON type the leaf coerces to (invariant culture). auto maps natively (numbers stay numbers, temporal values become ISO 8601 strings, binary becomes base64); json parses the source string and embeds the structure (a GeoJSON column).
.NET format string for $type: date (default yyyy-MM-dd) or $type: dateTime (default ISO 8601). Rejected on any other type.
What the leaf emits when its source value is NULL. 'default' requires $default; a present $default alone implies it.
The constant emitted under $whenNull: default (any YAML shape).

Directive array: one element per row of the named dataset whose bind columns match the enclosing scope ('rows' iterates the primary result at documents.per: resultSet). Takes exactly $forEach + $item.

Directive single-row block (the header / one-to-one counterpart of $forEach): the named dataset must resolve to EXACTLY one row at the enclosing scope (a bind-less header dataset, a bound one-to-one child, or 'rows' when the primary result is one row at documents.per: resultSet); $item renders once in that row's scope. Zero or several matching rows fail the run with the count. Takes exactly $row + $item.
The body of a $forEach array (one element per matching row) or a $row block (rendered once), with the dataset row pushed onto the scope (child columns shadow same-named enclosing columns).

The destination folder: a local path (relative resolves against the flow file), file:// URI, or Azure Blob/ADLS URI. Always written: the saved files are the durable record; the invoke step delivers exactly what was saved.

The layout: one .json file per document, one .jsonl file (one compact document per line), or one .json file holding a single array. Single-file modes write their file even for zero documents (deterministic overwrite: the destination mirrors the latest truth).

The file name (no extension). {Column} tokens (per-document mode with per: row only) render per document with filesystem-hostile characters sanitized; a rendered collision fails the run. A tokenless per-document name gets the document number appended.
Append _yyyyMMddHHmmss to single-file names so runs land side by side instead of overwriting. Off by default: deterministic overwrite is the contract.
Pretty-print (filePerDocument/array). Rejected on jsonLines: a JSON Lines document is one compact line.

The delivery URL (invoke: itself is optional; url is required within it). Supports ${...} secret references, and {Column} tokens from each document's root row when output.mode is filePerDocument with documents.per: row and batchSize 1.
The HTTP method, uppercased.
Extra request headers; values may carry ${...} secret references. Content-Type defaults to application/json unless declared here.

HTTP authentication: the exact same surface as an api flow's source.auth (none, apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery, bearer, basic, oAuth2ClientCredentials, oAuth2RefreshToken, tokenExchange with a token: block).

Documents per request: 1 posts each document as its own body; above 1 posts JSON arrays of up to this many. Applies to filePerDocument and jsonLines; an array output always posts as one request (declaring a batchSize there fails).
Wrap each request's documents in an envelope object under this key (OSDU's {"records": [...]}). The wrapped body is always an array, even for one document.

The exact same surface as an api flow's source.reliability: timeoutSeconds, retry (maxAttempts/baseDelayMs/maxDelayMs/honorRetryAfter), rateLimitRps, maxResponseBytes, verifyTls, urlAllowlist, skipStatusCodes (per-request tolerated non-2xx), and concurrency (default 1 here: in-order delivery unless the flow opts into parallel requests).
